en.greeting: Hi! Today we travel back in time: we imagine a different past, and how it would change things then and now. Let's start!

steps.title: Imagine a different past
steps.text: Quick recap: **first** = real (*If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home*), **second** = imagined now (*If I had more time, I would learn Japanese*). Now: an imagined **past**.
steps.body:
To imagine a past that **didn't happen**, use the **third conditional**:
**if + had + third form**, **would have + third form**
*If I had known about the meeting, I would have come.* = I **didn't** know, and I **didn't** come.
Why *had known*, not *knew*? *If I knew* already means **now** (second conditional), so for the past the verb goes **one more step back**.
Indonesian uses words (*seandainya dulu, kalau saja waktu itu*); English changes the **verb**.

pairs.en: What would you have done if …?
pairs.id: Apa yang akan kamu lakukan seandainya waktu itu …?

steps.title: It didn't happen
steps.text: In every sentence, both parts are **untrue**: they're a different version of the past.
steps.body: Look for the past time and the two parts: **had + third form** after *if*, **would have + third form** in the result. Negative: **hadn't**, **wouldn't have**.

examples.en: If I had known about the meeting, I would have come.
examples.id: Seandainya waktu itu saya tahu soal rapatnya, saya pasti datang.

examples.en: If we hadn't missed the bus, we wouldn't have been late.
examples.id: Kalau saja kami tidak ketinggalan bus, kami tidak akan terlambat.

examples.en: If Pak Hasan had read the email, he would have sent the report on time.
examples.id: Seandainya Pak Hasan membaca emailnya, dia pasti mengirim laporannya tepat waktu.

examples.en: What would you have done if you had lost your passport in Singapore?
examples.id: Apa yang akan kamu lakukan seandainya waktu itu paspormu hilang di Singapura?

steps.title: A missed train
steps.text: Pak Hasan didn't hear his alarm this morning, so he missed the 7:00 KRL and was late for work.

question.prompt: Complete: If Pak Hasan ___ his alarm, he wouldn't have missed the train.
question.explanation: This morning is the **past**, and it didn't happen, so the if-part needs **had + third form**: *had heard*. *heard* (past simple) would make it about now, and *would* never goes after *if*.

steps.title: Two traps, and could / might have
steps.text: Indonesian *seandainya dulu* has no tense, and *akan* covers will and would. That causes two typical mistakes.
steps.body:
**1. No past simple in the if-part:** 'If I knew about it, I would have come' ✗ → **If I had known** ✓.
**2. No would in the if-part:** 'If I would have studied harder' ✗ → **If I had studied harder** ✓. (Heard in casual American speech, but not standard.)
After *have*, the **third form**: *would have gone*, not 'would have went'.
In the result you can also use **could have** (it was possible, *bisa*) or **might have** (maybe, *mungkin*).

steps.title: A forgotten birthday
steps.text: Rina: 'It was my birthday yesterday!' You didn't know. You say: 'Oh no, sorry! If I had known, …'

question.prompt: Finish your reply. Arrange the words: saya pasti membawakanmu hadiah.
question.solution: I would have brought you a present.
question.explanation: The result of an imagined past: **would have + third form** (*bring → brought → brought*). You didn't know, so you didn't bring a present.

steps.title: 'd = had or would?
steps.text: In speech, **had** and **would** both become **'d**: *If I'd known, I'd have come.* Here's how to tell them apart.
steps.body:
Look at the word **after** 'd:
- **'d + third form** (*known, gone, been*) → **had**: *I'd known* = I had known
- **'d + have + third form** → **would**: *I'd have come* = I would have come
- **'d + base verb** → **would**: *I'd like*
In the **if-part**, 'd is always **had** (no would after if).
*would have* is said fast: *would've* ('wud-ev'). Write **would have** or **would've**, never 'would of'.

steps.title: Listen to Dimas
steps.text: Dimas got very wet on his motorbike yesterday. Listen to what he says.

question.prompt: Listen. Which sentence means the same as what Dimas says?
question.listen: If I'd known it was raining, I'd have taken the car.
options: If I had known it was raining, I would have taken the car.
If I would know it was raining, I had taken the car.
If I had known it was raining, I had taken the car.
question.explanation: *I'd known*: 'd + third form, in the if-part → **had**. *I'd have taken*: 'd + have + third form → **would**. So: *If I had known …, I would have taken the car.*

steps.title: Mixed: a different past, a different now
steps.text: Sometimes a past choice changes your life **now**. Then you mix the two conditionals.
steps.body:
**if + had + third form** (imagined past), **would + base verb** (imagined now):
*If I had studied IT, I would have a different job now.*
For something happening now: **would be + -ing**. Trap: 'I would be live in Jakarta now' ✗ → **would be living** or **would live** ✓.
The **time words** decide: *now, today, still* → **would + base verb**; *yesterday, last year, in 2019* → **would have + third form**.
Less often, the other way round: *If I spoke Japanese, I would have applied for that job last year.*

steps.title: A lawyer who loves computers
steps.text: Dimas studied law, not IT. Now he's a lawyer in Jakarta, and he's bored. He has always loved computers.

question.prompt: Complete: If Dimas had studied IT, he ___ at a tech startup now.
question.explanation: An imagined past (*had studied*) with a result **now** → a mixed conditional: **would be + -ing** (or *would work*). 'would be work' joins *be* and the base verb, and *would have worked* is a past result, which doesn't fit *now*.

steps.title: The scholarship
steps.text: In 2020 Sari turned down a scholarship to study in the UK. Today her English still isn't very good.

question.prompt: Complete: If Sari had accepted the scholarship, she ___ fluent in English now.
question.explanation: The if-part is the past (2020), but **now** puts the result in the present → **would + base verb**: *would be*. *would have been* is a past result, and *will* doesn't fit an imagined situation.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's the whole lesson on one page. Keep it for the next time you imagine a different past!

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Third & mixed conditionals
artifact.intro: Third conditional = if + had + third form, would have + third form, for an imagined past. Mixed = if + had + third form, would + base verb, for a past change with a result now.
rows: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.
If I had more time, I would learn Japanese.
if + had + third form, would have + third form
If I had known about the meeting, I would have come.
If we hadn't missed the bus, we wouldn't have been late.
could have / might have + third form
If she'd asked me, I could have helped her.
What would you have done if …?
What would you have done if you had lost your passport?
If I'd known … = If I had known …
I'd have come = I would have come
if + had + third form, would + verb
If I had studied IT, I would have a different job now.
If I had taken that job, I would be living in Jakarta now.
if + past, would have + third form
If I spoke Japanese, I would have applied for that job last year.
tips: **No would after if**, and no past simple for the past: *If I had known*, not *If I knew* / *If I would have known*.
**Time words decide:** *yesterday, last year* → would have + third form; *now, today, still* → would + base verb.
*would be live* ✗ → **would be living** / **would live** ✓. Write *would have* / *would've*, never *would of*.

examples.en: If I had known about the meeting, I would have come.
examples.id: Seandainya waktu itu saya tahu soal rapatnya, saya pasti datang.

examples.en: If she'd asked me, I could have helped her.
examples.id: Seandainya dulu dia minta tolong, saya bisa membantunya.

examples.en: If I had studied IT, I would have a different job now.
examples.id: Seandainya dulu saya kuliah IT, sekarang pekerjaan saya pasti lain.

steps.title: Watch and read
steps.text: Want more? Watch two short BBC videos, one on the third conditional and one on mixed conditionals, and read the British Council page with two grammar tests.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita kembali ke masa lalu: membayangkan masa lalu yang berbeda, dan bagaimana itu mengubah keadaan, dulu maupun sekarang. Ayo mulai!

steps.title: Membayangkan masa lalu yang berbeda
steps.text: Ulasan singkat: **first** = nyata (*If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home*), **second** = khayalan sekarang (*If I had more time, I would learn Japanese*). Sekarang: **masa lalu** khayalan.
steps.body:
Untuk membayangkan masa lalu yang **tidak terjadi**, pakai **third conditional**:
**if + had + bentuk ketiga**, **would have + bentuk ketiga**
*If I had known about the meeting, I would have come.* = saya **tidak** tahu, dan saya **tidak** datang.
Kenapa *had known*, bukan *knew*? *If I knew* sudah berarti **sekarang** (second conditional), jadi untuk masa lalu kata kerjanya **mundur satu langkah lagi**.
Bahasa Indonesia memakai kata (*seandainya dulu, kalau saja waktu itu*); bahasa Inggris mengubah **kata kerjanya**.

pairs.en: What would you have done if …?
pairs.id: Apa yang akan kamu lakukan seandainya waktu itu …?

steps.title: Kenyataannya tidak terjadi
steps.text: Di setiap kalimat, kedua bagiannya **tidak nyata**: ini versi lain dari masa lalu.
steps.body: Perhatikan waktu lampaunya dan kedua bagiannya: **had + bentuk ketiga** setelah *if*, **would have + bentuk ketiga** di bagian hasil. Negatif: **hadn't**, **wouldn't have**.

examples.en: If I had known about the meeting, I would have come.
examples.id: Seandainya waktu itu saya tahu soal rapatnya, saya pasti datang.

examples.en: If we hadn't missed the bus, we wouldn't have been late.
examples.id: Kalau saja kami tidak ketinggalan bus, kami tidak akan terlambat.

examples.en: If Pak Hasan had read the email, he would have sent the report on time.
examples.id: Seandainya Pak Hasan membaca emailnya, dia pasti mengirim laporannya tepat waktu.

examples.en: What would you have done if you had lost your passport in Singapore?
examples.id: Apa yang akan kamu lakukan seandainya waktu itu paspormu hilang di Singapura?

steps.title: Ketinggalan kereta
steps.text: Pak Hasan tidak mendengar alarmnya tadi pagi, jadi dia ketinggalan KRL jam 7.00 dan terlambat ke kantor.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: If Pak Hasan ___ his alarm, he wouldn't have missed the train.
question.explanation: Tadi pagi itu **masa lalu**, dan kejadiannya tidak terjadi, jadi bagian if perlu **had + bentuk ketiga**: *had heard*. *heard* (past simple) membuatnya jadi tentang sekarang, dan *would* tidak pernah dipakai setelah *if*.

steps.title: Dua jebakan, serta could / might have
steps.text: *Seandainya dulu* dalam bahasa Indonesia tidak punya tense, dan *akan* mencakup will dan would. Ini menyebabkan dua kesalahan yang sering terjadi.
steps.body:
**1. Jangan pakai past simple di bagian if:** 'If I knew about it, I would have come' ✗ → **If I had known** ✓.
**2. Jangan pakai would di bagian if:** 'If I would have studied harder' ✗ → **If I had studied harder** ✓. (Terdengar dalam bahasa Inggris Amerika yang santai, tapi tidak baku.)
Setelah *have*, pakai **bentuk ketiga**: *would have gone*, bukan 'would have went'.
Di bagian hasil kamu juga bisa pakai **could have** (waktu itu *bisa*) atau **might have** (*mungkin*).

steps.title: Lupa ulang tahun
steps.text: Rina: 'It was my birthday yesterday!' Kamu tidak tahu. Kamu bilang: 'Oh no, sorry! If I had known, …'

question.prompt: Selesaikan jawabanmu. Susun kata-katanya: saya pasti membawakanmu hadiah.
question.solution: I would have brought you a present.
question.explanation: Hasil dari masa lalu khayalan: **would have + bentuk ketiga** (*bring → brought → brought*). Kamu tidak tahu, jadi kamu tidak membawa hadiah.

steps.title: 'd = had atau would?
steps.text: Saat bicara, **had** dan **would** sama-sama jadi **'d**: *If I'd known, I'd have come.* Begini cara membedakannya.
steps.body:
Lihat kata **setelah** 'd:
- **'d + bentuk ketiga** (*known, gone, been*) → **had**: *I'd known* = I had known
- **'d + have + bentuk ketiga** → **would**: *I'd have come* = I would have come
- **'d + kata kerja dasar** → **would**: *I'd like*
Di **bagian if**, 'd selalu **had** (tidak ada would setelah if).
*would have* diucapkan cepat: *would've* ('wud-ev'). Tulis **would have** atau **would've**, jangan 'would of'.

steps.title: Dengarkan Dimas
steps.text: Kemarin Dimas basah kuyup naik motor. Dengarkan apa yang dia katakan.

question.prompt: Dengarkan. Kalimat mana yang artinya sama dengan ucapan Dimas?
question.listen: If I'd known it was raining, I'd have taken the car.
options: If I had known it was raining, I would have taken the car.
If I would know it was raining, I had taken the car.
If I had known it was raining, I had taken the car.
question.explanation: *I'd known*: 'd + bentuk ketiga, di bagian if → **had**. *I'd have taken*: 'd + have + bentuk ketiga → **would**. Jadi: *If I had known …, I would have taken the car.*

steps.title: Mixed: masa lalu berbeda, masa kini berbeda
steps.text: Kadang pilihan di masa lalu mengubah hidupmu **sekarang**. Kalau begitu, kamu mencampur dua conditional.
steps.body:
**if + had + bentuk ketiga** (masa lalu khayalan), **would + kata kerja dasar** (sekarang, khayalan):
*If I had studied IT, I would have a different job now.*
Untuk sesuatu yang sedang berlangsung sekarang: **would be + -ing**. Jebakan: 'I would be live in Jakarta now' ✗ → **would be living** atau **would live** ✓.
**Kata waktu** yang menentukan: *now, today, still* → **would + kata kerja dasar**; *yesterday, last year, in 2019* → **would have + bentuk ketiga**.
Lebih jarang, kebalikannya: *If I spoke Japanese, I would have applied for that job last year.*

steps.title: Pengacara yang suka komputer
steps.text: Dimas kuliah hukum, bukan IT. Sekarang dia pengacara di Jakarta, dan dia bosan. Dari dulu dia suka komputer.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: If Dimas had studied IT, he ___ at a tech startup now.
question.explanation: Masa lalu khayalan (*had studied*) dengan akibat **sekarang** → mixed conditional: **would be + -ing** (atau *would work*). 'would be work' menggabungkan *be* dengan kata kerja dasar, dan *would have worked* adalah akibat di masa lalu, tidak cocok dengan *now*.

steps.title: Beasiswa
steps.text: Tahun 2020 Sari menolak beasiswa kuliah di Inggris. Sekarang bahasa Inggrisnya masih belum terlalu bagus.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: If Sari had accepted the scholarship, she ___ fluent in English now.
question.explanation: Bagian if-nya masa lalu (2020), tapi **now** membuat akibatnya di masa kini → **would + kata kerja dasar**: *would be*. *would have been* adalah akibat di masa lalu, dan *will* tidak cocok untuk situasi khayalan.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini seluruh pelajaran dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk lain kali kamu membayangkan masa lalu yang berbeda!
